items.claim: Edges at a pin ELK couldn't hold keep ELK's route, label point and ports
items.note: This also covers an edge at a cluster that holds such a pin.

items.claim: A failed bundled-elkjs import is cached, so every later layout fails
A node and a cluster sharing an id get the same ELK id
items.note: I made the strict call: `elkPlan` now rejects any id shared by two participants or clusters, and that also catches two nodes with the same id. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: An edge label's `offset` is dropped, so ELK leaves room in the wrong place
items.note: ELK can't be told which side of the wire a label sits on, so a label with an offset now gets room centered on its wire, wide enough across the ranks for the label on either side. It reserves more space than the label needs.

items.claim: README documents `ElkPlan.groups`, but the field is `clusters`
items.note: which also changes the README's other "group" wording to "cluster".

items.claim: A reordering cluster's `ordered` member order never reaches ELK
items.note: as docs only. The README now lists it as "not taken". I checked elkjs 0.12 directly: per-cluster `forceNodeModelOrder` crashes it while it lays out every level at once (`INCLUDE_CHILDREN`), and `inLayerSuccOf`, `positionChoiceConstraint` and semi-interactive `elk.position` are ignored. The only option that works applies to the whole graph and would reorder clusters that didn't ask for it.

items.claim: A failed first load of elkjs's bundled build is cached, so every later layout fails too
`minimumTransposed` misses direction and hierarchy spellings ELK accepts, so a cluster's `minWidth` lands on the wrong axis
A cluster's `ordered` member order is silently dropped
README documents `ElkPlan.groups`, but the field is `clusters`
A label's `offset` is dropped on the ELK path, so ELK leaves no room for the gap the label is drawn at
`elkPlanner(opts)` lets an explicitly `undefined` field erase the run's option
